title: Single sign-on through the household's provider, for Octave on every platform
description: Serves "Joining and signing in are easy and safe.". One provider declared in configuration. Passkeys and second factors come from it (D-119). Octave on Android TV and phones, and Octave Web, sign in through it by a one-time code bound to the device that started (absorbs JS-180, #296).
acceptanceCriteria: Octave on Android TV (approved from a phone, JS-191) and on an Android phone signs in through the provider and plays; the device holds its own sign-in, with the session, watch state and access of a password sign-in.

The provider's tokens never reach Octave. The return carries only a one-time code that expires in about 60 seconds. The code is redeemed once, by the verifier of the device or tab that started the sign-in, and a second redemption or a wrong verifier is refused.
The journey is over HTTPS only. With real processes, start, return and redemption are each answered by a different api replica. A threat review of the handoff is recorded before Build.

A first sign-in links the local user whose name equals the provider's username claim, a migrated user without a password included, and keeps its watch state. After that the subject is the identity, and email never links.

Provisioning is a configuration switch, off by default. On, an unmatched first sign-in creates a viewer with the policy a new local user gets; off, it is refused with its reason on the page and in the log.
A user disabled or deleted in jellyscale is refused through the provider too. Removal at the provider stops new sign-ins only, and docs/access.md says so.
The journey's routes are bounded per address. The client secret comes from the environment and is never in configuration or logs.
Every capability it adds is in the published contract (JS-183) and passes its conformance check.
notes: Needs its own guessing bound, following JS-145's design (product owner, 2026-11-19). Reopens to 30 (after Quick Connect) if a household with an identity provider is waiting or reports it. Refine returns a brief before Spec on whether an administrator may be linked by name, since whoever picks a name at the provider takes that account. No device-authorization grant (rejected as a second protocol; a QR, if it comes, is Quick Connect's code in a link, its own task after this one). Refine designs the return so that no token or reusable code appears in a URL, and so that JS-180 is a second form of the same handoff, not a second protocol. #296: for Octave Web, redeeming the one-time code sets up the web sign-in (JS-215), so no credential readable by the page is handed out.
